subject: desertOasisDiorama
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: desert oasis with palms, tents and camels.
Style: low-poly whimsical mix.
reasoning:
I'm planning a low-poly desert oasis diorama with palms, tents, and camels, aiming to keep it under a reasonable part budget using the builder SDK's joint and part creation calls I'm confident are correct.

To stay safe, I'll skip the premade kits and instead hand-build surfacing with paint, stripes, and spot patterns, plus SVG textures for the tent fabric, rather than relying on toon kit utilities I'm less sure about.

For scale, I'm planning a modest diorama around 4 meters wide, with a sand base built as a cylinder for the dune floor rather than a more complex lathe profile, keeping a root joint at the origin and treating the camels as mostly static geometry rather than fully rigged.

Actually, since creatures should be skeleton-first, I'll give camels a moderate rig: a hips joint for the body, a chain for the neck leading to a head joint, and sweep-based legs attached to hip-level joints, keeping the chain setup simple with one parent per segment.

Defining leg chain joints...

For tents, I'm thinking of using a four-sided cone geometry rotated 45 degrees to make a pyramid shape, then applying a striped cream paint pattern across it.

I'm planning the tent entrance as a dark box on the front face plus a pole, and for palms building a tapered sweep trunk with bark rings and fronds made from extruded leaf outlines radiating from the crown.

Still working out frond geometry...

Now shifting to the camel: sweeping a tapered torso shape along a catmull-rom spine with an added hump profile.

I'm also roughing out face details using small spheres positioned at local head coordinates for eyes, figuring out the right local-space convention for placement.

For texturing I'll draw on the full palette—noise, stripes, spots, countershading, grain, mottling, cell patterns, gradients, paint—and add an SVG banner texture on a plane for the tent's door pattern.

Now I'm working out vertical placement: sand top sits at y=0.3 with objects resting there, and the model's base stays grounded at y=0. For the oasis pool, I'm placing a flattened water-colored cylinder on top of the sand but need to figure out how to sink it into the sand surface rather than floating above it, using a rim to blend the edge.

Still working out the rim geometry...

Now I'm adding palm trees around the oasis pool at offsets from center, then sketching sand dunes as flattened, scaled spheres partially sunk into the ground for texture.

Next I'm working out camel proportions—setting a ground offset and positioning the body, hump, and legs so hooves land correctly on the sand surface.

I realize the rig can only have a single root joint across the whole model, so all camels and palms need to be children of one shared root, with each creature's hip joint parented to it explicitly. I also need to think about joint orientation defaults — without an aim, a joint just inherits its parent's orientation, so I'll need to set that explicitly where it matters.

For the camel body, I'm planning a swept sweep along a spine path from tail to neck using a varying radius function to create the barrel shape, skinned rigidly to the hips bone with a countershaded coat texture, then adding a hump as a separate sphere piece.

Now I'm building the neck as a chain of catmull-spline joints parented to the hips, swept with a tapering radius profile, and attaching the head as a joint parented to the neck's final bone.

Now I'm planning the four legs as joint chains from hip to knee to hoof, with front legs positioned further forward and rear legs back, feet resting near ground level around y=0.3.

Adding hips joint for rear legs, then building camel details — tail sweep with tuft, a colored saddle rug on the hump with striped paint, and eye spheres positioned on the head. Then I'll start the tent shape using a cone for the pyramid form.

I'm figuring out the tent door placement—adding a small dark box near the front face of the cone and working out the geometry so it sits flush against the sloped pyramid-like surface at the right height.

Adding tent rotation helpers and pole/finial details...

For the palm, I'm curving the trunk with a tapering radius and bark ring texture, attaching it to a base joint, and setting up a crown joint at the top where eight fronds radiate outward at evenly spaced angles with drooping leaf shapes.

Defining frond outlines...

Now I'm adding scene details: coconuts as small brown spheres near the crown, oasis greenery with simple shrub spheres, a couple of flattened dodecahedron rocks, and a lathe-based amphora for water jars, plus rug and crate props. I'm leaning into a whimsical bright palette (turquoise, pink, orange) for tents and camel humps, settling on three standing camels with varied yaw and colors for simplicity, and adding a sun sphere to the scene.

I'm defining the full color palette for sand, water, palm foliage, tents, camel coats, and ink, then building paint functions: mottled sand textures, countershaded camel coats, striped rugs and tents, and mottled turquoise water, along with the ground ring and a possible banner texture plane.

For the tent decoration, I'm adding a small SVG-textured trim plane above the door with a zigzag pattern, oriented to face forward, plus starting to lathe a jar profile for stacked jar props.

Now I'm writing a rotation helper function that converts local x/z offsets by a yaw angle into world coordinates relative to a base position, so parts can be placed correctly around each rotated object.

Adding joint positioning helper...

Working out joint naming and chain structure for neck, head, and leg attachments, then starting on the tail sweep geometry with its own catmull path points.

Now I'm sizing up the body sweep's shape—checking that the radius profile and bottom edge still clear the legs, and confirming leg placement along the body width so everything lines up proportionally.

Then I'm placing the legs for a camel: rear and front positions with a slight forward bow in the path, plus hoof cylinders sized to just touch the ground plane. For the head, I'm building a boxy snout shape positioned at the neck joint, adding small cone ears and sphere eyes, and checking that the neck-to-head transition sits naturally.

Now I'm adding a hump as a flattened sphere on the hips, and a saddle rug as a thin box positioned just above the body surface with yaw rotation to match the body curve, keeping extra decorations like tassels minimal to avoid clutter.

Moving on to palm trees, I'm writing a helper function that builds each trunk as a curved sweep with a tapering radius, topped by a crown joint that fronds attach to, keeping the trunk itself rigid to the root bone.

Still writing frond placement logic...

Adjusting the lower edge points so they stay consistently below the upper edge at each corresponding u position along the frond.

I'm giving leaves a slight thickness and bevel, then adding coconuts as small spheres near the crown, varying frond colors between two shades of green for visual interest. For the oasis, I'm scattering icosahedron-based shrubs around the sand near the pool.

Rocks and dunes use scaled icosahedrons and spheres respectively, while jars are built with a lathe function that takes an outline, position, and color. For banner trims, I'm designing an SVG texture with zigzag triangle patterns in red and gold tones.

Still writing SVG triangles...

For the tent structure, I'm placing a trim plane above the door and planning the tent body as a low-poly cone with four radial segments for that angular, faceted look.

With the 45-degree rotation, faces end up axis-aligned facing ±x and ±z, so I'm placing the door along the +Z face. I'm working out the door's world position by computing the tent surface distance at the door's height, setting its center around y=0.5 with a small offset so it sits flush against the sloped wall.

I realize the vertical door box doesn't match the sloped tent face geometrically—it would either poke through or sit recessed depending on height, so I'm reconsidering the approach: maybe tilt the door box to match the slope angle, or simplify by switching to a flat-faced prism tent shape to avoid the issue altogether.

Actually, a cleaner solution: build the tent as an extruded gable prism (triangular cross-section stretched along z), and build the door as a separate dark triangular extrusion placed flush on the front face, avoiding the slope-matching problem entirely.

Now I'm shaping the tent body itself: a triangular-ended prism with a pointed ridge, extruded along the length, and considering whether to add horizontal stripe bands across the fabric for the circus-tent look.

I'm thinking about topping the apex with a small pole and pennant flag, then arranging a few of these tents at different yaw angles around the oasis pool for variety.

Now I'm planning the overall layout: a ground disc base, with a pool at the center and palm trees and tents positioned around it at specific offsets so nothing overlaps.

I'm defining a helper transform that converts local camel coordinates into world positions by rotating around each camel's base point and keeping height absolute, so I can place multiple camels at different spots and orientations consistently.

Now I'm sketching rough camel placements around the pool, checking distances and yaw angles so they don't overlap the pool rim while still facing varied directions toward or away from the viewer, without worrying about exact precision.

Tents should sit around 1.3 units out on the 4.8m diorama disc, with camels roughly 2.2m tall and palms around 2.6m, matching real-world proportions. Now I'm starting the code with the necessary imports from the builder library, double-checking which helper functions like noise and mottle are actually exported.

Setting up the meta export and color palette...

Still defining color palette...

Now I'm defining the pool using a lathe profile to create a rounded stone basin, with a mottled rock texture applied and checking the default segment smoothing settings.

I'm adding a thin cylinder as the water surface sitting just inside the basin rim, then starting to build out a palm tree generator function that takes position, lean angle, height, and seed to procedurally create the trunk path.

Writing trunk sweep and crown joint...

Now I'm generating the frond geometry, looping through a set of leaf shapes radiating outward at varying angles and lengths with randomized jitter for a natural palm look.

I'll type the leaf array as a union of tuple shapes to satisfy the outline point type, then write the extrude call positioning the leaf at the frond tip with thickness and bevel for a rounded shape, alternating between two leaf colors.

Adding coconut spheres clustered near the crown...

Still working through the palm placement parameters and starting on the tent structure definitions...

Writing the tent body extrusion with alternating color bands...

Working through the cross product confirms the extrusion direction points forward along the ridge, which checks out. Now I'm sketching the outline coordinates for the stripe pattern and the door shape with its peaked top.

I'll settle on a dark plum color for the door, then add a trim banner plane positioned above it, textured and rotated to face forward using the same yaw rotation logic as the door.

Adding ridge trim sweep...

Now I'm adding a gold pole finial with a small spike shape at the tent top, then working out a triangular pennant flag to attach near the spike tip.

With the tent structure done, I'm adding interior touches: colored cushions near the entrance and a striped rug box placed and rotated to match the tent's yaw. Next I'm starting a camel-building function, sketching its parameters for position, orientation, and coat color.

Writing camel joint hierarchy...

Finalizing the tail taper formula, then adding a hump sphere positioned to sit atop the body, and starting a rug box shape placed on the hips.

Settling on a rug size and position with minor clipping accepted since it's a stylized build, then moving to the neck, which I'm building as a two-joint chain following a curved path from the hips up to the head area.

Next I'm sweeping the neck with a tapering radius, then adding the head joint without an explicit aim so it inherits the neck's orientation, keeping things simple. For the head geometry, I'm sketching out a skull box, a snout box offset forward, and ears as spike shapes, all using yaw-only rotation for simplicity.

Still writing geometry...

Now I'm setting up eyes, nose, and the leg chains, defining spline control points for front and back legs parented to the hips using Catmull-Rom curves.

Adding sweep profile and hoof...

Placing three camels with varied positions, rotations, and coat color tones for visual variety.

Checking camel 0's head and rear positions against the disk boundary - both fit comfortably within radius. Camel 1's head position comes close to the 2.3 edge at roughly 2.15 distance, so I may need to nudge its placement slightly inward to stay safe.

Moving on to adjusting camel 1 to (-0.9,0.7) with a shallower yaw of 20 degrees for better fit. I'm now working out camel 2's forward vector and tail position at yaw 160, then placing the two tents - one warm cream/red toned tent on the left, one teal/cream tent on the right - while positioning three leaning palm trees to fill out the scene, checking that nothing overlaps with the camels already placed.

I'm setting up a cleaner coordinate system so tent heights are measured as absolute offsets above the ground plane rather than relative to a shifting base, which should simplify the math considerably compared to the camel calculations I already did.

Now I'm placing the pool and palm trunks at ground level, then scattering several rocks randomly within a disk around the center using a seeded approach so the layout stays consistent.

I'm sinking the rocks slightly into the ground with flattened scale and a mottled stone color, clustering small green shrubs near the pool edge, and setting up lathe-based jars with striped paint near tent A using a defined profile shape.

Now I'm adding a small helper for degree-to-radian conversion and a rotation function that positions objects at an offset and yaw angle relative to a base point.

Generating trim texture SVG...

Setting up per-tent paint with two color variants, and considering whether to add glowing lanterns at tent doors—though without an emissive material in the kit, I'll likely skip the glow and just keep a simple lantern stick if anything.

Now I'm sketching out palm tree placement coordinates and checking that each one sits clear of the pool rim and tent bodies, roughly verifying distances so nothing overlaps.

I'm then repositioning the camels and tents to avoid collisions: shifting camel0 near (1.05,1.05) with a yaw adjustment, moving tent B to roughly (1.6,-0.35), nudging palm1 slightly, and placing camel1 and camel2 at separate spots, double-checking the gaps between each pair stay safely apart before placing jars near tent A's front.

I also want to scatter shrubs around the pool rim at a safe radius, add a dune and some rocks, and keep the total part count reasonable. Then I'll verify the type consistency across lathe, part, and paint options, and settle on using countershade with specific level and softness values for the camel's coat and belly coloring before applying the same pattern to the hump.

Now I'm ready to write the whole module compactly, making sure the joint chain is set up correctly with the root joint and proper parenting, then deliver the answer with a brief intro.
